data.name: HelpText
data.value:
CamaroDiag Windows J2534 Bridge — command line Run without arguments to open the graphical interface.
Usage: CamaroDiag.J2534Bridge.exe --help CamaroDiag.J2534Bridge.exe --list-ports CamaroDiag.J2534Bridge.exe --self-test CamaroDiag.J2534Bridge.exe --probe-drivers CamaroDiag.J2534Bridge.exe --discover-connector COM5 CamaroDiag.J2534Bridge.exe --inspect-connector-checkpoint checkpoint.bin CamaroDiag.J2534Bridge.exe --inspect-write-journal attempt.jsonl CamaroDiag.J2534Bridge.exe --inspect-e39-image original-3MiB.bin CamaroDiag.J2534Bridge.exe --port 35001 CamaroDiag.J2534Bridge.exe --port 35001 --memory-read-profile profile.json CamaroDiag.J2534Bridge.exe --port 35001 --allow-obd-clear
Examples: --self-test Software simulation only. No ECU or adapter. --probe-drivers Inspect installed Windows J2534 drivers; no ECU. --discover-connector COM5 USB serial CD/1 discovery only, isolated prototype. --inspect-write-journal attempt.jsonl Inspect an offline write journal; never recover or erase. --port 35001 Start the TLS-paired LAN bridge using a selected J2534 driver. It may check for app updates; never forward the LAN port to the Internet. --allow-obd-clear Explicitly enable OBD DTC clear on this local bridge run. The Android user must also confirm OK then YES.
Use each option with the exact arguments described above. --help must be alone: mixing it with a programming command fails without contacting hardware. Raw UDS, flash and EEPROM operations are NOT enabled by this help. A simulated pass does not qualify the device on a real ECU. Linux x64/ARM64 bridge and matching CLI remain planned in issue #115.
